sources.note: The phonology chapter (section 2.5 Word-accent, pp. 40-41) describes BACHAMAL/Batjamalh (batj1234), not Giyug: stem-initial syllable carries predictable high-pitch accent. On Giyug (called Kiyuk) it says only, p. 9: 'Agnes Lippo's step-father, Daly Young, was one of the last speakers of Kiyuk. Agnes remembers Kiyuk as mutually unintelligible with Bachamal. There is no-one left with even passive competence in Kiyuk.' Also pp. 4-5 (Kiyuk as western neighbours; Peron Islands custodianship inherited 'from the last of the Kiyuk') and p. 17 (Nipper Rankin, 'a Kiyuk man', could not speak Kiyuk). No…
